ai.definition: Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) technology enables electric vehicles to send electricity back to the grid during peak demand periods. This process involves using the vehicle's battery as a source of backup power.
ai.howItWorks: During off-peak hours, V2G-capable electric vehicles can charge their batteries from the grid. When energy demand peaks and prices rise, these vehicles can return stored energy to the grid through bidirectional charging systems. This process helps stabilize the electrical grid by providing additional supply during peak times.
ai.problemSolved: V2G technology addresses the challenge of balancing supply and demand in the power grid, particularly when integrating intermittent renewable sources like solar and wind into the system.
ai.manufacturing: Manufacturing V2G-capable vehicles involves integrating advanced battery management systems that can handle both charging from and discharging to the grid. This requires specialized components and software for bidirectional charging capabilities.
ai.buildProcess: The build process includes vehicle assembly with integrated V2G hardware, followed by software integration and testing of the bidirectional charging system.
ai.costDrivers: Key cost drivers include the development and certification of bidirectional charging systems, battery management technology, and the initial investment in vehicle infrastructure to support V2G operations.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The outlook for V2G is positive as more renewable energy sources come online and grid stability becomes increasingly important. However, widespread adoption will depend on regulatory frameworks and consumer acceptance.
ai.regulation: Regulatory support is crucial for the deployment of V2G technology. Policies that incentivize or mandate V2G participation can accelerate market penetration.
ai.risks: Technical risks include ensuring battery longevity and safety during frequent charge-discharge cycles, while economic risks involve the initial high cost of implementing V2G infrastructure and the variability in energy pricing models.
ai.profitability: Profitability is contingent on factors such as government incentives, energy price fluctuations, and the volume of vehicles participating in V2G programs. Early adopters may see higher returns due to subsidies and early market advantages.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future development could involve more advanced battery technologies that support deeper charge cycles without degradation, as well as improved grid management systems to optimize V2G operations.

glossary.def: A technology that allows electric vehicles to send electricity back to the power grid during peak demand periods.
The capability of an electrical vehicle's battery to both charge from and discharge energy to the grid.

subsystems.name: Bidirectional charger
subsystems.role: converts grid AC power to DC for the battery and back again, synchronising with the grid.

subsystems.name: Vehicle battery and BMS
subsystems.role: stores energy and manages safe charging and discharging.

subsystems.name: Communication and control
subsystems.role: lets vehicle, charger, aggregator and grid operator exchange signals.

subsystems.name: Aggregation platform
subsystems.role: pools many vehicles to act as a single grid resource.

subsystems.name: Grid interface and protection
subsystems.role: ensures safe connection to the distribution network.

buildSteps.title: Design bidirectional power electronics
buildSteps.detail: Develop a charger that can invert DC battery power to grid-synchronised AC and rectify AC to DC, with efficiency above 90%.

buildSteps.title: Implement communication standards
buildSteps.detail: Embed ISO 15118-20 or CHAdeMO protocols in vehicles and chargers so they can negotiate discharge rates and grid services.

buildSteps.title: Equip vehicles
buildSteps.detail: Install larger onboard chargers or use external chargers, and update battery management firmware to allow controlled discharge without excessive degradation.

buildSteps.title: Build aggregation software
buildSteps.detail: Create a platform that aggregates thousands of vehicles, forecasts availability, and bids into electricity markets or grid-operator schemes.

buildSteps.title: Deploy charging infrastructure
buildSteps.detail: Install bidirectional chargers at homes, workplaces and depots, with wiring and switchgear rated for two-way power flow.

buildSteps.title: Establish grid interconnection
buildSteps.detail: Work with utilities to set protection settings, metering arrangements and tariffs that allow and reward export to the grid.

buildSteps.title: Run pilot fleets
buildSteps.detail: Test V2G with buses, delivery vans and employee cars to validate technology, battery wear and revenue streams under real conditions.

buildSteps.title: Scale up manufacturing and markets
buildSteps.detail: Mass-produce bidirectional chargers, open grid markets to aggregated vehicles, and roll out to consumers.

prerequisites.why: chargers exist but are costly and not yet mass-produced for homes or small fleets.
ISO 15118-20 and CHAdeMO support it, but implementation across vehicles and chargers is uneven.
some regions allow small-scale export, but many lack standards for aggregated vehicle power.
pilot aggregators exist, but electricity markets rarely accept small, mobile resources at scale.
more cycling may shorten battery life; long-term data is still limited.
advanced metering and grid sensors are widely deployed in many countries.

pathway.milestone: pilot projects with fleet vehicles (buses, delivery vans) provide grid services
pathway.unlocks: real-world data on battery wear and revenue.

pathway.milestone: commercial V2G for fleets and workplace charging, with aggregators selling frequency response
pathway.unlocks: a viable business case for businesses with parked vehicles.

pathway.milestone: residential V2G available with bidirectional home chargers and supportive tariffs
pathway.unlocks: household backup power and lower energy bills.

pathway.milestone: widespread V2G integrated into grid markets, providing large-scale storage and backup
pathway.unlocks: cheaper integration of variable renewables, reducing need for dedicated batteries.
